product: commentary — no product. The AI debate split-screen method (scaling CBO winners).
hook: "Almost every winner in our scaling CBO this month is AI debate."
body: Six-step method: (1) debate, not interview — arguments feel like skits; (2) extreme character contrast (younger girl vs old man, karen vs gen-z skater); (3) outside environment, not podcast; (4) controversial ragebait layer; (5) split screen beats camera switching; (6) format transition — put the debate character in a podcast. Copied from an agency where it underperformed; crushing for them since.
idea: Split-screen AI debates with extreme character contrast and ragebait.
why_it_works: Arguments hold attention — viewers stay to see who "wins"; split screen keeps both faces in frame.
what_to_steal: Split-screen debates for LC: "cheap jewelry girl vs LC girl" arguing — contrast plus split screen, minus the ragebait.

product: commentary — no product. The desire-first argument (split screen as one wrapper among three).
body: No format is the clear winner — what's tested is desire, not format. Pick the desire first (relief from complexity, fear of falling behind, looking put-together); the format stops mattering. Three wrappers, one desire: founder explaining one solution vs seven, split screen of old routine vs new, throwing out six bottles. Test the desire before the wrapper or the winner teaches nothing reusable.
idea: Test desire before wrapper — split screen is just one outfit for the same desire.
why_it_works: Desire-level learnings transfer across formats; format-level learnings don't.
what_to_steal: For LC split screens: define the desire first ("look put-together effortlessly"), then shoot the old-routine-vs-new split screen.

product: commentary — no product. Split-screen reading-reviews format (Q4 prep series part 1/4).
body: Split screen (reading reviews + b-roll) as one of the most engaging ways to put real customer feedback into an ad; the example ran for months past Black Friday because it kept selling. 55s video attached.
cta: "follow so you don't miss the next format breakdowns."
idea: Split screen lets reviews play over b-roll — social proof with motion.
sequencing: Split screen: reading reviews plus b-roll.
One of the most engaging ways to use real feedback.
Ran for months past Black Friday.
why_it_works: Real reviews carry trust; b-roll carries attention — split screen delivers both at once.
what_to_steal: LC split screen: 5-star reviews on one side, jewelry b-roll/macro shots on the other — LC has 74k+ verified reviews to mine.
